question: If the front tire suddenly goes flat while riding, the steering will feel:
explanation: If the front tire goes flat, the steering will feel 'heavy,' and it is particularly hazardous because it affects steering and balance.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.35, 'Tire Failure'

question: If the rear tire goes flat while riding, the back of the motorcycle may:
choice_b: Jerk or sway from side to side
explanation: If the rear tire goes flat, the back of the motorcycle may jerk or sway from side to side.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.35, 'Tire Failure'

question: If a tire goes flat while riding, if braking is required, the manual advises to:
choice_a: Apply both brakes fully and immediately
choice_b: Only apply the rear brake, regardless of which tire failed
choice_c: Gradually apply the brake of the tire that is not flat, if you are sure which one it is
explanation: If braking is required with a flat tire, gradually apply the brake of the tire that is not flat, if you are sure which one it is, then edge to the side and stop.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.35-36, 'Tire Failure'

question: If the throttle becomes stuck, the manual's first recommended action is to:
choice_d: Twist the throttle back and forth several times to try to free it
explanation: Twist the throttle back and forth several times; if the cable is stuck, this may free it.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.36, 'Stuck Throttle'

question: If the throttle stays stuck after trying to free it, the rider should:
choice_a: Operate the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time
choice_b: Continue riding normally, since the engine will eventually stall
explanation: If the throttle stays stuck, immediately operate the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch to remove power from the rear wheel.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.36, 'Stuck Throttle'

question: A 'wobble' is best described as:
choice_a: A slow drift to one side of the lane
choice_b: The front wheel and handlebars suddenly shaking side to side at any speed
choice_c: A gradual loss of engine power
choice_d: The rear wheel bouncing over bumps
explanation: A wobble occurs when the front wheel and handlebars suddenly start to shake from side to side at any speed.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.36, 'Wobble'

question: If a wobble occurs, the manual specifically warns riders NOT to:
choice_c: Apply the brakes, since it could make the wobble worse
choice_d: Move their weight forward and down
explanation: Do not apply the brakes during a wobble, since braking could make the wobble worse; close the throttle gradually instead.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.36-37, 'Wobble'

question: Trying to 'accelerate out of a wobble' will:
explanation: Trying to accelerate out of a wobble will only make the motorcycle more unstable.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.37, 'Wobble'

question: A chain or belt that slips or breaks while riding could cause:
choice_a: An instant loss of power to the rear wheel
choice_b: A sudden increase in top speed
explanation: If the chain or belt breaks, you will notice an instant loss of power to the rear wheel; close the throttle and brake to a stop in a safe area.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.37, 'Drive Train Problems'

question: Engine seizure, when the engine 'locks' or 'freezes,' is usually caused by:
explanation: When the engine locks or freezes, it is usually low on oil; the moving parts can't move smoothly and the engine overheats.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.37, 'Engine Seizure'

question: If engine seizure is suspected, the rider should first:
choice_a: Accelerate to reach a service station quickly
choice_b: Downshift repeatedly to restart engine power
choice_c: Squeeze the clutch lever to disengage the engine from the rear wheel, then pull off and stop
choice_d: Ignore it since it will resolve itself
explanation: Squeeze the clutch lever to disengage the engine from the rear wheel, pull off the road and stop, and check the oil.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.37, 'Engine Seizure'
